text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: prefix-cache hitrate drop >40% in us-west-2 (2026-03-15T14:02Z). Severity: P1. Pager: @sam park. Impact: elevated latencies for text-gen routes and 5xx for some customers.

sam park: Oncall here, looking. Any customer-facing incidents yet?

leah ortiz: Yep, support stack reporting increase in 502s for /v1/generate from two customers in us-west. Dashboard: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/cache/hitrate?region=us-west

jp chen: Attaching quick timeline from observability:
- 13:48Z: deploy of cache-indexer 2.9.1 rolled to canary (small).
- 13:55Z: batching config sync to prod (prefix-split enabled).
- 13:59Z: error rate and latency start trending up.

jp chen: Logs (sample from cache node cache-07):
```
[2026-03-15T13:59:12Z] prefix_lookup miss key="usr:prefix:abc123" shard=7
[2026-03-15T13:59:12Z] eviction triggered: keys=1024 freed=128 cause=ttl_sync
[2026-03-15T13:59:13Z] kv_reuse=false prefix=usr:prefix:abc123
[2026-03-15T13:59:15Z] rewarm-scheduler queued=0 backlog=512
```

aisha khan: That eviction pattern looks like a TTL sync gap. Hitrate falls when large amounts of keys are invalidated. Could be the indexer change + TTL migration race.

maria gomez: Reproduced on staging: enabling prefix-split with the existing TTL map caused intermittent prefix key mismatch leading to misses. I have a repro script.

sam park: Immediate mitigation ideas? Can we bump TTLs or pause indexer rollout?

eng-sre: Propose immediate actions: 1) pause prefix-split rollout 2) increase soft TTL on caches to 15m 3) enable temporary warmup for hot prefixes

leah ortiz: On it. Pausing rollout now. `kubectl patch deployment cache-indexer -n infra -p '{"spec":{"paused":true}}'` -> DONE.

jp chen: Bumping TTL on cache cluster now: `cachectl set-ttl --cluster us-west --ttl 900` -> executing.

incident-bot: Action logged: pause-deployment cache-indexer (user=leah ortiz) at 14:06Z; set-ttl 900 (user=jp chen) at 14:07Z.

aisha khan: After TTL bump, hitrate started recovering 14:11Z but still ~10% below baseline. Need rewarm for hot prefixes.

maria gomez: Starting rewarm job for top 100 prefixes: `jobs/rewarm-top-prefixes --region us-west --count 100` -> queued.

sam park: Can we confirm customer impact window and affected keys for the RCA? Support asked for timeline and which customers saw 5xx.

jp chen: Customer impact (from logs):
- cust-A: errors 13:59Z-14:10Z
- cust-B: errors 14:02Z-14:09Z
Linked error traces: https://traces.internal/redwood/trace/abc123

leah ortiz: Noting downstream effect: some frontend retries flooded the cache tier causing transient connection errors; we saw connection backpressure on cache nodes (net:conn_drops).

eng-sre: Collecting artifacts for RCA: cache logs (shards 0-15), indexer deploy manifest, TTL migration changelog, rewarm job logs, APM traces. Put in /incidents/2487654321/artifacts (privileged access).

jp chen: Hypotheses (track):
- H1: indexer prefix-split rollback logic mismatch caused stale prefix map -> massive misses -> eviction storm. (evidence: timing with deploy + prefix_lookup misses).
- H2: TTL migration job raced with indexer, causing mass TTL resets and eviction. (evidence: eviction cause=ttl_sync in logs).
- H3: rewarm scheduler backlog is mis-sized causing delayed warmup after invalidation. (evidence: rewarm-scheduler queued=0 backlog=512).

maria gomez: I'm assigning myself to H1 verification, aisha to H2, jp to H3.

sam park: Good. Also we should capture hit-rate time series and per-prefix QPS for the window. @aisha can you grab per-prefix qps?

aisha khan: Running query: `select prefix, sum(ops) from cache.metrics where ts >= '2026-03-15T13:45Z' and ts <= '2026-03-15T14:30Z' group by prefix order by sum(ops) desc limit 200` -> results uploading to artifacts.

jp chen: Rewarm job completed for top 100 prefixes at 14:20Z, hitrate back to ~98% by 14:22Z. No further customer 5xx after 14:25Z.

leah ortiz: Noting mitigation timeline for postmortem:
- 13:48Z canary deploy indexer 2.9.1
- 13:55Z batch config sync (prefix-split enabled)
- 13:59Z hitrate drop begins
- 14:04Z pager -> oncall sam
- 14:06Z pause indexer rollout (leah)
- 14:07Z TTL bump to 900s (jp)
- 14:12Z rewarm job started (maria)
- 14:22Z hitrate recovery to baseline
- 14:25Z first customer 5xx resolved

sam park: Ok. Next steps during incident: keep channel for artifacts & timeline. For RCA we need: root cause statement, evidence mapping to H1/H2/H3, long-term mitigations, runbook updates.

maria gomez: Early root cause draft: "race between prefix-indexer rollout and TTL migration produced an inconsistent prefix->TTL mapping causing mass prefix invalidations and eviction storms; rewarm backlog and small soft TTL amplified customer impact."

aisha khan: Agree. Proposed long-term fixes: stronger rollout gating (canary traffic validation), transactional TTL update with indexer, increase rewarm concurrency and prioritized hot-prefix warmers.

eng-sre: Also add a metric alert guard: if global cache hitrate drops >20% for >2min, auto-pause indexer rollouts and notify oncall.

jp chen: I'll open the RCA doc and populate timeline/evidence. Action items: JP - rewarm tuning PR, Maria - indexer rollback verification and test, Aisha - TTL migration transactional patch, Leah - add alert and rollback automation playbook.

sam park: Great. If no more urgent updates, we'll hand off to the RCA owners. I'll remain the incident lead until the RCA doc is complete.

incident-bot: Incident state changed -> mitigated (user=sam park) at 14:30Z. Please set status to postmortem when ready. :white_check_mark:

leah ortiz: Thanks team. I'll ping support with customer impact summary and ETA for RCA doc. :thumbsup:

jp chen: Uploading logs + queries now. Closing live mitigation channel, moving to #incidents-postmortem for RCA drafting.

maria gomez: saved repro and testcases under artifacts/repro-2487654321.zip

sam park: Closing channel for live ops. RCA owners, flag if you need more data.

leah ortiz: Closing out. :lock:
